missingColumnsPolicy: The 51 columns the datamodel declares but the production database lacks are all nullable or defaulted (verified by scripts/pg/drift-report.mjs, which reports zero required-without-default columns over existing rows). The importer simply omits them and Postgres applies the default.

Job.invoiceNumber.finding: 13 invoice numbers appear on more than one Job (15 surplus rows). Production has no Job_invoiceNumber_key index, so the duplicates were never rejected. The job numbers involved come from different months (EIS-4/2026/0020, EIS-5/2026/0020, EI-2026-0020), which points at a document-numbering sequence collision rather than genuine duplicate invoicing.
Job.invoiceNumber.resolution: Job.invoiceNumber is a denormalised copy; the Invoice table is authoritative and its own invoiceNumber values are unique with no duplicates. For each duplicated number there is exactly one Invoice row and it references exactly one Job. Keep the value on that job; set it to NULL on the others. No Invoice, Payment or Receipt row is touched.

DocumentBrandingSettings.orgId.finding: Two branding rows carry orgId=org_eis_01: the legacy id='singleton' row (updated 2026-04-11) and the per-org id='org_eis_01' row (updated 2026-06-06).
DocumentBrandingSettings.orgId.resolution: Keep orgId on the per-org row, which is authoritative and newer. Set orgId to NULL on the legacy singleton, which keeps it readable as the fallback that lib/document-branding.ts still looks for by id.

Job.why: 15 surplus duplicates cleared by the job-invoice-number resolver; invoiceNumber is not numeric so no sum is affected

DocumentBrandingSettings.why: legacy singleton's orgId cleared by the branding-singleton resolver

Receipt.why: orphaned payment ids nulled by the nullOrphan policy — see orphanPolicy

Receipt.paymentId.finding: Two receipts point at a Payment.id that is not in the dump: EIS/RCT/2026/0029 (UGX 650,000) and EIS/RCT/2026/0030 (UGX 450,000). Both are already voided, both carry voidReason "Payment deleted", and both were voided within 40 minutes of being issued on 2026-08-30. The payments were deleted in the application; SQLite enforced no foreign keys, so the dangling id string stayed behind.
Receipt.paymentId.decision: Null Receipt.paymentId on those two rows. The datamodel declares the relation onDelete: SetNull with a nullable column, so this is not a repair but a replay: had the delete gone through Postgres, the database would have nulled the column itself. Nothing is lost — the receipt, its number, amount, invoice link, issuer, void reason and void timestamp all import unchanged, and the void reason already records where the payment went.
Receipt.paymentId.rejected: Skipping the two receipt rows. They are real issued-then-voided documents inside a numbered sequence; dropping them would leave two gaps in EIS/RCT/2026 that nothing explains.

Expense.paidAmount.finding: Expense.paidAmount and the ExpensePayment table arrived from main after the dump was taken, so no dump carries the column. Every imported expense lands on its default of 0, including the 14 whose paidAt records them as settled — which reads as fully owing everywhere payables is calculated.
Expense.paidAmount.decision: After the rows are written, set paidAmount = amount wherever paidAt is not null. The guard paidAmount < amount keeps it idempotent and leaves genuine part-payments alone, so re-running an import never overwrites a balance the application itself recorded.
Expense.paidAmount.rejected: Leaving it to the migration alone. prisma migrate deploy runs against an empty database at cutover, so its backfill updates nothing and the import that follows reintroduces the zeros. That is exactly how the development database lost the backfill once already.

dumps.mrms-prod-2.db: 2026-09-12 — the dump this map is currently verified against

missingOnly.finding: Live was loaded from a dump taken 2026-10-26, and the old Turso database kept taking writes afterwards. A full re-import would destroy what has been entered on live since; the rows created on the old system in the meantime have to be added to a database that is in use.
missingOnly.decision: Add, never change. A row is written only if its id is absent from the target and it is either a new top-level record (`roots`, created after --created-after) or belongs to a record written in the same run. Anything whose unique number is already taken on the target, or whose parent could not be written, is skipped and listed. Existing rows are never updated: rows edited on the old system after the cutoff are listed for a person to merge.

never.why: Sessions, notifications and logs are not business records. OutboundMessage rows in a retryable state would be sent again by the retry job. Stock movements cannot be added without adjusting quantities the target has moved on from. Counters are reconciled by Data Heal, not copied. Users and organisations are created by the app.

missingOnly.polymorphicNote: These columns point at their owner without a foreign key, sometimes as `kind:id`. A row is treated as belonging to a record written in this run when the id part matches one.

sameAs.why: A client is identified by phone number within an organisation; the datamodel makes the pair unique. When a client was entered on both systems after the cutoff, the two rows are the same customer under different ids. The incoming row is not written and the target's row is not changed; jobs, devices, invoices and quotations that pointed at the incoming row are attached to the target's. Without this an invoice arrives with no client and the customer's jobs are skipped.

stampedNumbers.why: A job carries a copy of its invoice number. When that number already belongs to a different invoice on the target, the job's own invoice is skipped as a clash — and writing the job with the stamp intact would leave a job and an unrelated invoice sharing one number, which is the duplicate Data Heal exists to undo. The stamp is cleared instead and reported, so the invoice is re-issued on the target under a number it owns.
